Hi Alex / Priya —

Great to meet today. Quick recap + proposed next steps on the reliability/SLO items you asked us to clarify (and how Redwood compares to the hyperscalers):

Notes from the call:
- Primary evaluation focus: uptime guarantees, rate limiting behavior, error budget calculation, and failover semantics during regional or model failures.
- You're running a competitive eval that includes Vertex/AWS and want apples-to-apples load/failover tests next week.
- Goal is to validate tail latency and failover behavior under sustained load and when we inject model timeouts.

Where Redwood stands (summary):
- Hosted API: production-grade but multi-tenant; soft default limits and regional routing. We expose rate-limit headers, Retry-After semantics, and provide traffic shaping recommendations.
- Dedicated: SLA-backed pools (99.95% uptime typical for reserved pools), predictable throughput (reserved GPUs), and isolated error budgets. Suitable if you need strict SLOs.
- Failover: smart routing + automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity or a region is degraded. We surface logs and traces for retries/fallback events.

Proposed next tests (so we can compare to Vertex/AWS):
1) Load test: ramp to 500 req/s sustained for 2 hours against a representative prompt set, capture p50/p95/p99 latency and error rates.
2) Burst/Rate-limit test: spike to 2x expected burst to validate 429 behavior + Retry-After and client backoff handling.
3) Failover test: simulate regional outage (route to alternate region) and inject model timeouts to verify fallback to lightweight variant and measure added latency.
4) Error-budget calc: run 7-day synthetic traffic to compute % of requests outside agreed p95 threshold and map to error budget.

Requested from you: can you confirm the test windows/dates and whether you want us to run the load drivers (we can run them and share scripts) or you prefer to run on your side?

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (SOC 2 snapshot), architecture-failover-diagram.png, test-plan-loadscript.yaml (draft).

Next steps / owners:
- Ben: coordinate schedules and provide load scripts if you want Redwood to run tests.
- Rishi: will provide SLO specifics and expected headers/metrics to collect.
- Marissa: will follow up on pricing for Dedicated pool if test shows we meet targets.

Thanks — available for a quick sync if you'd like to walk through the test plan live.

Hi Alex — quick technical write-up to help you compare behavior against Vertex/AWS and to support the test plan.

Hosted vs Dedicated (numbers):
- Hosted (multi-tenant): default soft limits are 300 req/s for standard REST generation endpoints per org. Burst handling: short bursts up to ~1k req/s allowed but subject to smoothing and 429s if sustained.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): scales to thousands of req/s depending on pool size; we provision capacity per contract so you don't see tenant-level cross-traffic.
- Token guidance: we recommend token-based budgeting for cost but rate-limits are enforced on request rates (requests/sec) for sequencing/latency guarantees.

429 / 503 semantics and retry guidance:
- On 429 we return Retry-After (seconds) and an X-Redwood-Quota-Reset header. Clients should implement exponential backoff with jitter; suggested policy: initial retry after Retry-After, then 2^n * base with max cap 30s.
- On 503/timeouts we return a structured error with request id; our client SDK surfaces this and recommends immediate failover logic if a configured threshold of consecutive 503s (default 5 within 60s) is reached.
- Circuit breaker: recommended client-side threshold is 5 x 503 within 60s or 10% error rate over a sliding 1m window. We can tune this with you.

Failover & fallback behavior:
- Routing: health checks + automated routing policy reroutes traffic to the next healthy region; expected detection time depends on failure mode but is typically 30–90s for regional failure.
- Model fallback: on model variant failure or capacity shortage we will route to a pre-configured compatible smaller variant. Latency impact is workload dependent; ballpark +50–200ms on top of normal p95 for many workloads, but measured impact will vary based on model size and prompt length.
- Observability: all fallback events emit trace IDs and an event in the route-level dashboard. We will share a sample query for logs and a short Kibana/Grafana link you can use for the test.

SLO / error budget calculation:
- Example SLA: Dedicated pool SLA 99.95% availability monthly.
- Error budget = 1 - SLA (e.g., 0.0005 of total minutes per month). We'll share the math and a script to compute error budget burn given your p95/p99 measurements.

Test plan notes (what we'll provide):
- Loadscript (JMeter/locust) + seed prompts.
- Expected headers to capture: X-Redwood-Request-Id, X-Redwood-Region, X-Redwood-Fallback, Retry-After, X-Redwood-Quota-Reset.
- Dashboard queries for p50/p95/p99 and fallback/error counts.

Attachments: test-plan-loadscript.yaml (draft). I can join the run to help interpret results and trigger failover scenarios safely.

Let us know whether you want Redwood to run the load or if you'll run it. If you're running, please provide the public IP range we should expect so we can pre-allow traffic for Dedicated pool tests.
